subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Anal canal, small bowel and appendiceal cancers

steps.tx: Anal canal squamous cell carcinoma is predominantly driven by high-risk human papillomavirus HPV infection, particularly genotypes **16** and **18**. HPV oncoproteins E6 and E7 inactivate tumour suppressors p53 and retinoblastoma protein respectively, leading to chromosomal instability, high p16INK4a overexpression, and exquisite sensitivity to definitive radiation and DNA-damaging cytotoxic agents.

nodes.label: Definitive IMRT (45 to 54 Gy) Concurrent Chemo
Clinical Assessment at 26 Weeks for Complete Response

edges: Mitomycin C on Day 1 and Day 29

steps.tx: The **Nigro protocol** combining external beam radiotherapy with concurrent 5-fluorouracil and mitomycin C achieves **organ preservation** in over 70% of localized anal carcinomas. This landmark definitive chemoradiotherapy approach preserves functional anal sphincter mechanism while yielding 5-year local disease control and overall survival rates equivalent or superior to primary radical surgical extirpation.

left.title: Complete Clinical Response
points: Complete disappearance of palpable and visible mass by 26 weeks
Normal digital rectal examination and anoscopy
Resolution of metabolic activity on PET-CT scan
Requires routine surveillance every 3-6 months for 5 years

right.title: Persistent / Recurrent Disease
points: Biopsy-proven invasive squamous carcinoma at >= 26 weeks
En-bloc resection of rectum, anus, and sphincter complex

steps.tx: Abdominoperineal resection with permanent end colostomy is reserved as radical **salvage therapy** for persistent or locally recurrent anal cancer following definitive chemoradiotherapy. Clinical response assessment should be deferred until 26 weeks post-chemoradiation due to delayed tumour clearance; premature intervention at 12 weeks risks performing morbid salvage therapy on healing tissues.

rows: Median OS 20.0 vs 12.3 mo; lower serious adverse events (36% vs 62%)
ORR 24%; approved in refractory HPV-associated anal SCC
Long-term disease control in isolated liver or lung metastases

steps.tx: Small bowel adenocarcinoma is an uncommon luminal malignancy frequently diagnosed at advanced stages with unique anatomical distribution. **Small bowel adenocarcinoma** predominantly arises in the **duodenum**, with high rates of microsatellite instability MSI-H and mismatch repair deficiency dMMR secondary to Lynch syndrome or underlying Crohn disease. Genomic profiling demonstrates high frequencies of KRAS, TP53, and SMAD4 mutations, sharing biological drivers with colorectal adenocarcinoma.

nodes.label: Underlying Predisposition: Lynch Syndrome or Crohn Disease

edges: Often presents with occult GI bleeding

steps.tx: Systemic antineoplastic therapy for unresectable small bowel adenocarcinoma mirrors protocols established in advanced colorectal cancer. Systemic therapy for advanced unresectable small bowel adenocarcinoma utilizes fluoropyrimidine-oxaliplatin doublets **mFOLFOX6 or CAPOX**, while deficient mismatch repair dMMR tumours demonstrate marked responsiveness to **pembrolizumab**. In BALLAD and prospective registry studies, platinum-based regimens established median overall survival of twelve to sixteen months in microsatellite-stable disease.

rows: FOLFIRI or FOLFIRINOX; limited EGFR inhibitor activity

steps.tx: Malignant epithelial neoplasms of the appendix exhibit distinct biological behaviour dictating specialized multimodal management. Appendiceal low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms LAMN can rupture, seeding the peritoneal cavity to cause **pseudomyxoma peritonei** PMP, characterized by gelatinous ascites and redistribution to the greater omentum and diaphragmatic surfaces. PMP lacks significant haematogenous or lymphatic dissemination, remaining confined exclusively to the peritoneal surface.

left.title: Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm (LAMN)
points: Pushing, non-infiltrative growth with mucin extrusion
Slow progression with voluminous acellular mucin production
Excellent long-term survival following complete cytoreduction

right.title: High-Grade Appendiceal Adenocarcinoma
points: Destructive infiltrative invasion with signet-ring cells
High propensity for nodal and haematogenous distant spread
Forms aggressive peritoneal carcinomatosis with high PCI
Requires systemic chemotherapy in addition to cytoreduction

steps.tx: Locoregional eradication of peritoneal dissemination requires aggressive surgical debulking paired with intraperitoneal heated chemotherapy. Curative-intent management of pseudomyxoma peritonei comprises **complete cytoreductive surgery** CRS achieving completeness of cytoreduction score CC-0/1 combined with **hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy** HIPEC utilizing heated mitomycin C or oxaliplatin. CRS involves systematic peritonectomies and visceral resections to remove all macroscopic mucinous deposits.

nodes.label: Circulate Mitomycin C for 60 to 90 Minutes

steps.tx: **Ampullary carcinomas** arise from the **ampulla of Vater** and are histopathologically classified into intestinal and pancreatobiliary subtypes, dictating distinct adjuvant chemotherapy selections. Intestinal-type ampullary carcinomas behave like colorectal cancer and benefit from adjuvant fluoropyrimidine-oxaliplatin doublets, whereas pancreatobiliary-type tumours follow pancreatic protocols, managed with gemcitabine or capecitabine.

rows: Classic neuroendocrine cells with salt-and-pepper chromatin
Amphicrine cells: mucin-filled goblet cells + neuroendocrine IHC
Synaptophysin positive focal, CEA positive, CK20 positive
Indolent, cures with appendicectomy if < 2 cm
Aggressive local infiltration, peritoneal and nodal metastasis

steps.tx: Ampullary carcinoma arises at the ampulla of Vater and often presents early with **obstructive jaundice**, which can allow earlier detection than pancreatic head tumours. Surgical resection, usually pancreaticoduodenectomy, is the main curative option. Adjuvant therapy is considered based on stage and histology.
